messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: unit vectors
parts:
First, what's the motivation behind reparameterizing unit
vectors as

y / sum(y^2)?

It looks like the parameters won't be identifiable on the unconstrained
scale. Won't this be bad for adaptation and convergence monitoring
of the unconstrained parameters?

Second, if zero is a problem for initialization, would
it be feasible to assign the symmetric unit vector

1 / sqrt(size(y))

It's the limit of epsilon * (1, ..., 1) as epsilon -> 0.
(Of course, other angles of approach give different limits!).

- Bob

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] unit vectors
parts:
Unit vectors will never be identifiable until we move past the assumption
that all of our parameters live in R^{n}. Mathematically this is somewhat
straightforward (there’s a reason I keep all the HMC papers as general
as possible!) but there are all kinds of side effects (means and other
summary statistics are really hard to define on spaces like spheres and
torii).

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: unit vectors
parts:
On Thursday, December 3, 2015 at 2:53:54 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
First, what's the motivation behind reparameterizing unit
vectors  as

  y / sum(y^2)?

In the issue, I put the link to the last time we discussed refactoring this

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-dev/0cXoSwAs3tw/dPT-fAVojdIJ

It looks like the parameters won't be identifiable on the unconstrained
scale.  Won't this be bad for adaptation and convergence monitoring
of the unconstrained parameters?

The unconstrained parameters are identified by the prior assumption that y is i.i.d. standard normal, in which case x = y / sum(y^2) is uniform on the surface of the N-hypersphere and then you could (probably in rare circumstances) make the distribution non-uniform with a sampling statement for x. In Stan < 2.9, using a unit_vector as a parameter would not compile but if it did, the unconstrained hyperspherical angles aren't identified because of the periodicity of the trig functions, but we were basically hoping that they would not wander outside of (-pi,pi) or whatever.

Second, if zero is a problem for initialization, would
it be feasible to assign the symmetric unit vector

  1 / sqrt(size(y))

It's the limit of epsilon * (1, ..., 1) as epsilon -> 0.
(Of course, other angles of approach give different limits!).

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] unit vectors
parts:
Thanks --- that jogged my memory.

I'd think the derivative would be 0.

Maybe a better alternative would be to do a slightly
different normalization, like

x + epsilon / sum(x + epsilon)

where, say epsilon = .01. It's enough to be arithmetically
stable, but not enough to seriously skew initialization.
Probably not a big deal --- I don't find myself initializing
to zero very much any more now that adaptation's better.

- Bob
